article.title: Why Product Labels Can Mislead Shoppers

paragraphs.en: Product labels help people compare goods, but they can also create impressions that are technically accurate yet misleading. A picture of fresh fruit may suggest that a drink contains substantial fruit, even when the ingredient list tells a different story. Large words such as natural or pure can attract attention without explaining what the terms mean. Consumers should distinguish an appealing design from evidence about a product's contents. The most useful question is not simply whether the headline is true. It is whether the complete presentation helps an ordinary shopper understand the product fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 商品標示能幫助比較，也可能製造技術上正確卻誤導的印象。新鮮水果圖片可能暗示飲料果汁含量很高，但成分表未必如此。「天然」「純粹」等大字可能吸引目光，卻沒有解釋定義。消費者應區分吸引人的設計與產品內容的證據。重要的不只是標題是否真實，而是整體呈現是否有助一般人公平理解商品。
paragraphs.ja: 商品ラベルは比較に役立つ一方、事実でも誤解を招く印象を作ることがある。果物の写真や「自然」「純粋」といった言葉だけでは中身を判断できない。デザインと根拠を区別し、表示全体を確認することが大切だ。

paragraphs.en: Selective emphasis is a common marketing technique. A snack may proudly announce that it contains no artificial coloring while providing less visible information about sugar or salt. The statement about coloring can be correct, but it does not answer every nutritional question. Similarly, a package may advertise an impressive amount of protein without clearly showing that the number refers to an unusually large serving. Comparing products becomes difficult when the measurement basis changes. A careful shopper checks serving size, ingredient order, and the information that is missing from the most prominent claim.
paragraphs.zh: 選擇性強調是常見行銷手法。零食可能大力宣稱沒有人工色素，卻不明顯呈現糖鹽資訊。色素聲明可能正確，但不代表回答了所有營養問題。包裝也可能強調蛋白質含量，卻未清楚說明數字來自特別大的份量。比較基準不同就難以公平比較。謹慎的購物者會確認份量、成分排序，以及醒目宣傳未提及的資訊。
paragraphs.ja: 都合のよい特徴だけを強調する手法はよくある。「人工着色料不使用」が事実でも糖分や塩分の問題は残る。タンパク質量も一食分の大きさによって印象が変わる。比較の基準と省略された情報を確かめたい。

paragraphs.en: Environmental claims require similar care. Green packaging, pictures of leaves, and words suggesting sustainability may make a product appear responsible. Yet those visual cues do not establish that its production uses fewer resources or that the packaging can be recycled locally. A meaningful claim should identify a specific environmental benefit, explain how it was measured, and disclose relevant limitations. Reducing the weight of a bottle, for example, does not automatically mean that the entire product has a smaller environmental footprint. Good information makes the scope of a claim understandable rather than encouraging shoppers to guess.
paragraphs.zh: 環境宣稱也需要謹慎。綠色包裝、葉子圖案及永續字眼可能讓商品看起來負責任，但不能證明製造耗用較少資源或包裝能在當地回收。有意義的聲明應指出具體環境效益、測量方式及限制。瓶子變輕不代表整個產品的環境足跡必然降低。好的資訊會讓聲明範圍清楚，而非要求購物者猜測。
paragraphs.ja: 環境表示にも注意が必要だ。緑色や葉の絵は環境への配慮を連想させるが、資源消費や地域での再利用可能性の証拠ではない。具体的な効果、測定方法、限界を確認することが重要だ。

paragraphs.en: Placement matters as much as wording. Important conditions may appear in small print on the back, while the front displays a bold promise. Shoppers often decide quickly, so a truthful disclaimer may not fully correct a strong first impression. Clear labeling should make essential qualifications easy to find. This is especially important for introductory offers that become more expensive later. An attractive monthly price may apply only to the first few months, while renewal conditions receive much less attention. Reading the entire offer before paying helps prevent unexpected costs and disappointment.
paragraphs.zh: 資訊放置位置和措辭同樣重要。重要條件可能藏在背面小字，正面卻展示醒目承諾。購物決策通常很快，真實的免責文字未必能修正第一印象。清楚標示應讓重要限制容易找到。這對日後變貴的入門優惠尤其重要。吸引人的月費可能只適用前幾個月，續約條件卻不醒目。付款前讀完整方案可避免意外支出。
paragraphs.ja: 文字の配置も重要だ。重要条件が裏面の小さな文字にあり、魅力的な約束だけが表面に目立つことがある。初回料金と更新後の料金を区別し、支払い前に条件全体を読む必要がある。

paragraphs.en: Price comparisons offer another example. A large container can look economical, but its price per unit may be higher than that of a smaller package on promotion. Consumers should compare the same measurement, such as price per hundred grams, rather than relying on package size. They should also ask whether they will use everything before it expires. A bargain is not a genuine saving when half of the product goes to waste. A realistic comparison considers the total amount paid, the quantity actually used, and the convenience of the purchase.
paragraphs.zh: 價格比較是另一個例子。大包裝看似划算，單位價格卻可能高於促銷的小包裝。消費者應使用相同指標，例如每百公克價格，而不是只看包裝大小。也要考慮到期前能否用完。若一半產品被丟掉，特價就未必是真正節省。實際比較須考量總支出、真正使用量及購買便利性。
paragraphs.ja: 大容量が必ず割安とは限らない。百グラム当たりなど同じ単位で比較する必要がある。使い切れず廃棄するなら安売りでも節約にならない。支払総額と実際に使う量を考えたい。

paragraphs.en: A practical method involves four steps. First, identify precisely what the label promises. Second, examine the ingredients, specifications, and conditions relevant to that promise. Third, compare alternatives using the same unit and time period. Finally, decide whether the advertised benefit matters for your own needs. Someone with a dietary restriction may reasonably prioritize details another shopper ignores. Critical reading does not require believing that every company is dishonest. It means refusing to let a single attractive phrase replace evidence. When shoppers develop this habit, labels become more useful tools for informed decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 實用方法有四步。首先確認標示究竟承諾什麼；其次檢查相關成分、規格與條件；第三使用相同單位和期間比較；最後判斷宣傳效益是否符合個人需求。有飲食限制的人可能合理地重視其他人忽略的細節。批判性閱讀不等於認定企業都不誠實，而是不讓一句漂亮口號取代證據。養成習慣後，標示才能成為知情決策的工具。
paragraphs.ja: 実践方法は四段階だ。主張を特定し、根拠となる原材料や条件を確認し、同じ単位と期間で比較し、自分に必要な利点か判断する。すべての企業を疑うのではなく、魅力的な一言を証拠の代わりにしない姿勢が大切だ。
